sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Constitutional Basis**: Article 265 of the Constitution mandates that 'No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law'.
• **Seventh Schedule Division**: Powers are demarcated under Union List (List I), State List (List II), and Concurrent List (List III).
• **Direct vs Indirect Taxes**: Direct taxes (e.g., Corporate Tax, Personal Income Tax) have incidence and impact on the same entity; Indirect taxes (e.g., GST, Customs Duty) can be shifted to consumers.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Tax-to-GDP ratio, tax elasticity, and buoyancy coefficients measuring revenue responsiveness to economic growth.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Urban vs Rural Tax Collection**: Direct tax collection is heavily skewed toward metropolitan hubs like Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi, and Chennai.
• **State-wise Variations**: High industrial and service-sector density states generate higher GST revenues, necessitating mechanisms like GST compensation cess and Finance Commission devolution.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: High share of indirect taxes leading to regressivity, base erosion, profit shifting (BEPS), and complex compliance.
• **Policy Interventions**: Faceless assessment, expansion of tax base via digital transactions, rationalization of corporate tax rates, and strengthening data analytics.

items.title: Mnemonic for Direct vs Indirect Taxes
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'C-W-I-P' for Direct (Corporate, Wealth, Income, Property) vs 'G-C-E' for Indirect (Goods, Customs, Excise).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Instantly separates direct wealth/income tax burdens from transactional consumption taxes.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Eliminates confusion when UPSC asks about tax incidence classifications.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember the Article sequence: 265 (No tax without law), 270 (Taxes levied and collected by Union and distributed between Union and States), 279A (GST Council), 280 (Finance Commission).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'GST is a destination-based tax collected by the Centre alone.' This is false; GST comprises CGST, SGST, and IGST, where SGST is collected by the respective states and IGST is shared between the Centre and the destination state.

Mains Value Addition: Use keywords like 'Fiscal Federalism', 'Cooperative & Competitive Federalism', 'Tax Buoyancy vs Elasticity', and quote the 15th Finance Commission parameters to elevate answers on public finance.

keyTakeaways: Taxation in India is strictly governed by constitutional provisions under the Seventh Schedule and Article 265.
The tax structure balances direct progressive taxes with indirect broad-based consumption taxes like GST.
Institutional mechanisms like the Finance Commission and GST Council are vital for maintaining fiscal harmony between the Centre and States.
